subject: anaesthesia
title: Anaesthesia Workstation: Gas Delivery, Breathing Circuits, and Soda Lime

steps.title: Workstation Pressure System Zones
steps.tx: **Anaesthesia workstation pressure systems** divide into three distinct operational pressure zones: the high-pressure system receives gas directly from cylinders at up to 137 bar; the intermediate-pressure system receives pipeline gas at 4 bar (400 kPa or 60 psi) or gas stepped down by first-stage regulators; and the low-pressure system extends downstream of flow control valves to the common gas outlet at near-atmospheric pressure.

steps.title: Rotameter Thorpe Tube Mechanics
steps.tx: **Thorpe tube rotameter flowmeters** feature variable-orifice vertical glass tubes with an internally tapered lumen that widens progressively toward the top. Gas entering from the bottom suspends a bobbin or float: at low flows, gas passage is laminar and governed by gas viscosity (Poiseuille law); at high flows, the orifice is wide, and turbulent flow is determined by gas density. Rotating skirted floats are read at the top edge, whereas spherical ball floats are read at their midpoint.

left.title: Rotating Skirted Bobbin Float
points: Fluted head spins continuously in laminar gas stream
Flow rate read precisely at upper horizontal rim
Sticking indicates dirt or static electrical charges

right.title: Spherical Ball Float
points: Simple non-rotating sphere suspended in gas flow
Flow rate read strictly at central equator of ball
Commonly encountered in transport and auxiliary flowmeters

steps.title: Workstation Safety Mechanisms
steps.tx: **Workstation hypoxic guard mechanisms** guarantee that oxygen concentration in the delivered fresh gas mixture never drops below 25 percent. The mechanical link-25 system or pneumatic ratio controller interlocks nitrous oxide and oxygen flow control spindles so that advancing nitrous oxide automatically drives the oxygen valve forward, while an audible Ritchie whistle sounds when oxygen supply pipeline pressure plummets below 2 bar.

steps.title: Desflurane Tec 6 Vaporizer
steps.tx: **Desflurane Tec 6 vaporizer engineering** differs radically from conventional variable-bypass plenum vaporizers because desflurane has an extraordinarily low boiling point of 22.8 degrees Celsius at atmospheric pressure. To prevent uncontrolled boiling and catastrophic overdosing, the Tec 6 electronically heats liquid desflurane to 39 degrees Celsius and pressurizes its chamber to 2 atmospheres (1,500 mmHg), injecting pure vapor directly into the fresh gas stream.

right.title: Heated Desflurane Tec 6 Vaporizer

steps.title: Mapleson Breathing Circuit Classification
steps.tx: **Mapleson breathing system classification** categorizes semi-closed circuits from A to F based on the spatial arrangement of the fresh gas inlet, reservoir bag, corrugated tubing, and adjustable pressure limiting (APL) valve. Mapleson A (Magill circuit) is the most efficient for spontaneous respiration, requiring fresh gas flow equal to alveolar minute ventilation (approximately 70 to 100 milliliters per kilogram per minute) to prevent rebreathing.

rows: Least efficient (demands FGF 2.5 to 3x minute volume)

steps.title: Bain Coaxial Circuit Features
steps.tx: **Bain coaxial circuit construction** represents a modified Mapleson D system where a narrow inner plastic tube delivers fresh gas directly to the patient airway connection, surrounded by a wider outer corrugated tube conveying exhaled gases back to the APL valve. Exhaled gases warm the incoming fresh gas, but crack rupture of the inner tube causes severe unrecognized dead space rebreathing and lethal hypercapnia (Pethick test detects inner tube disconnection).

steps.title: Circle System and Soda Lime
steps.tx: **Circle system CO2 absorption** enables closed and low-flow anaesthesia (fresh gas flows under 1 liter per minute), drastically economizing volatile anaesthetic agents while preserving airway humidity. Soda lime granules (80 percent calcium hydroxide, 4 percent sodium hydroxide, 1 percent potassium hydroxide, and 15 percent water) absorb exhaled carbon dioxide in an exothermic neutralization reaction, forming calcium carbonate and water.

rows: Dry absorbent promotes carbon monoxide production

steps.title: Compound A and Carbon Monoxide Risks
steps.tx: **Toxic degradation hazards of volatile agents** arise during interaction with carbon dioxide absorbents: sevoflurane reacts with dry alkaline absorbents containing strong bases to produce Compound A (fluoromethyl-2,2-difluoro-1-trifluoromethyl vinyl ether), which induces nephrotoxicity in rats, mandating fresh gas flows of at least 1 to 2 liters per minute. Conversely, desflurane and isoflurane exposed to desiccated Baralyme generate dangerous carboxyhaemoglobin-producing carbon monoxide.

Conversely, desflurane and isoflurane exposed to desiccated Baralyme generate dangerous carboxyhaemoglobin-producing carbon monoxide.

left.title: Compound A Generation
points: Reaction between sevoflurane and dry strong-base absorbents
Directly toxic to proximal renal tubule cells in rodent models
Prevented by maintaining fresh gas flow greater than 1-2 L/min

right.title: Carbon Monoxide Generation
points: Desflurane or isoflurane exposed to bone-dry alkaline absorbent
Binds hemoglobin with 200-fold affinity forming HbCO
Avoided by replacing desiccated absorbents and Monday flushes
